brand_memory.s4: Brand Memory: how Anomalia learns your voice, preferences, and what works.
brand_memory.s8: Brand Memory is how Anomalia remembers everything about your brand — your voice, your preferences, what works, and what to avoid. It's the reason Anomalia sounds more like you over time.
brand_memory.s11: — tone, style, words you use, words you avoid
brand_memory.s13: — "always use Italian", "no emojis in captions", "never mention competitors by name"
brand_memory.s15: — which post formats get the most engagement, which hashtags perform
brand_memory.s17: — corrections, feedback, and instructions you've given in chat
brand_memory.s19: — what your competitors do well, white space in your market
brand_memory.s21: Anomalia learns from everything you do:
brand_memory.s23: — the changes you make are the strongest signal of your voice. If you shorten a caption or remove emojis, Anomalia learns that preference.
brand_memory.s25: — every conversation is analysed for preferences and constraints. Tell Anomalia "I prefer a more formal tone" and it remembers.
brand_memory.s27: — patterns in what you approve teach Anomalia what you want.
brand_memory.s29: — insights about your market are saved for future use.
brand_memory.s30: You can also add knowledge directly in Studio — notes, guidelines, and reference material that Anomalia treats as ground truth.
brand_memory.s32: Every week, Anomalia reviews what it has learned and refines its memory:
brand_memory.s33: Preferences you've reinforced multiple times become stronger
brand_memory.s35: Conflicting information is flagged for you to resolve
brand_memory.s36: The result: after a few weeks, Anomalia's output feels like it came from your team, not from a generic AI.

content_library.s4: Content Library: Anomalia indexes your site pages and links to them from social posts.
content_library.s8: Anomalia reads your website and builds a library of your pages — blog posts, guides, product pages, resources. When it creates social posts, it links to the most relevant pages from your own site.
content_library.s10: Anomalia scans your sitemap and finds all your public pages
content_library.s11: Each page is read and scored for relevance — how useful it would be to link from a social post
content_library.s12: When creating posts, Anomalia picks the best pages to link to, rotating through them so the same page isn't shared twice in a row
content_library.s14: Blog articles, guides, resource pages, and product pages — anything substantial. Pages like your homepage, login, cart, or legal pages are automatically skipped.
content_library.s15: When you publish new content on your site, the library picks it up on the next scan.
content_library.s17: Your content library drives two things:
content_library.s19: — when Anomalia creates a post, it can link to a relevant blog article or resource from your site, driving traffic back to you
content_library.s21: — articles Anomalia writes for your blog include internal links to your existing pages, boosting your SEO
content_library.s22: You don't need to manage this manually. Anomalia reads your site, scores the pages, and picks the right ones automatically.

editorial_plan.s5: How Anomalia's editorial plan works: strategy, weekly planning, and content generation.
editorial_plan.s9: The editorial plan is Anomalia's strategic layer — it defines what to post, when, and why. Everything is a proposal: you approve, and Anomalia creates.
editorial_plan.s11: Anomalia studies your market, competitors, and audience. It produces a growth roadmap with phased goals — where to focus in the next 90 days, and how that evolves over 6 months.
editorial_plan.s12: The strategy adapts to your real results. If something isn't working, Anomalia proposes course corrections.
editorial_plan.s14: A week-by-week content plan with themed topics, platform mix, and posting cadence. You can:
editorial_plan.s18: — give feedback and Anomalia proposes changes
editorial_plan.s20: — give context for specific weeks (e.g. "we have a product launch on Tuesday")
editorial_plan.s24: Each week, Anomalia proposes content ideas — hooks, angles, and themes. You approve the ones you like, and Anomalia produces them into full posts with captions, images, and scheduling.
editorial_plan.s25: You can approve ideas one by one, or approve the whole batch at once.
editorial_plan.s28: A strategy and editorial plan appear in your dashboard.
editorial_plan.s30: One tap — from the app, email, or the CLI.
editorial_plan.s32: Full posts with captions, visuals, and timing.
editorial_plan.s34: Approve, edit, or regenerate. Then Anomalia publishes on schedule.

geo_audit.s5: GEO Audit: find out if AI assistants recommend your brand — and fix the gaps.
geo_audit.s9: When a potential customer asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI a question about your industry — does your brand come up? The GEO Audit answers that, and tells you exactly what to fix.
geo_audit.s10: GEO = SEO for the AI era.
geo_audit.s11: Traditional SEO gets you into Google's list of links. GEO gets you into the AI-generated answer itself.
geo_audit.s13: The audit scans your website for everything that affects whether AI assistants can find, understand, and recommend your brand:
geo_audit.s15: — is your content clear, structured, and substantial enough for AI to cite?
geo_audit.s17: — can AI crawlers access your site, or are they blocked?
geo_audit.s19: — does your site have the metadata AI engines use to understand your business?
geo_audit.s21: — FAQ sections, images with descriptions, clear headings
geo_audit.s23: You get a score from 0 to 100 that reflects how easy it is for AI to recommend your brand. Each issue found is categorised by severity so you know what to fix first.
geo_audit.s24: AI presence: are you in the answer?
geo_audit.s25: The audit goes beyond your website. It asks real questions a buyer would ask — like "best CRM for small businesses" or "alternatives to [competitor]" — and checks whether AI mentions your brand in the answer.
geo_audit.s27: How often your brand appears in AI answers (your "share of voice")
geo_audit.s28: Which competitors are being recommended instead
geo_audit.s31: For every gap found, Anomalia generates copy-paste assets you can add to your site:
geo_audit.s33: — with the structured data AI engines love to cite
geo_audit.s35: — the metadata that helps AI understand your company
geo_audit.s37: — a special page that tells AI exactly what you do
geo_audit.s38: Anomalia proposes, you review and publish. The fixes are designed to slot into your existing site without redesigning anything.
geo_audit.s40: the audit runs weekly for all active brands. As you fix issues, your score improves.

post_history.s22: Posting frequency matches your natural cadence

seo_advisor.s4: SEO Growth Advisor: get a prioritised list of content initiatives to grow your organic search traffic.
seo_advisor.s8: Analyses your brand's organic search potential and produces a prioritised list of content initiatives — blog posts, landing pages, tools, comparison pages — each targeting a real search query your customers are making.
seo_advisor.s10: the advisor gives you directional demand — real competitors, realistic queries — not exact search volumes. For precise numbers, you'd need tools like Google Search Console or Ahrefs.
seo_advisor.s12: Two data sources feed the plan:
seo_advisor.s14: — where your brand is missing from AI answers, and what your competitors are doing
seo_advisor.s16: — what real customers search, which content formats win, and where the white space is
seo_advisor.s17: You get a qualitative evaluation of your current state, plus 5-8 prioritised initiatives ranked by effort and impact.
seo_advisor.s19: Each initiative is a concrete content idea:
seo_advisor.s23: — pages built for one specific topic
seo_advisor.s25: — calculators or utilities that attract organic traffic
seo_advisor.s27: — "X vs Y" pages that capture high-intent searches
seo_advisor.s29: — definition hubs that become reference material
seo_advisor.s30: Each one includes the target query, why it matters, and concrete examples.
seo_advisor.s32: One click on any initiative generates a ready-to-use asset — an article outline, landing page copy, or tool specification. You review, edit, and publish on your site.
seo_advisor.s34: you can also ask the chatbot for more ideas — "suggest blog topics about sustainable fashion" — and the results are added to your plan.

thematic_calendar.s3: Thematic Calendar: timely moments and events your brand can post about.
thematic_calendar.s7: Surfaces upcoming moments — holidays, seasonal events, industry happenings — that your brand could authentically post about. The planner uses these to add timely content to your editorial plan.
thematic_calendar.s9: Anomalia looks at your brand's category, audience, and region to find upcoming moments that genuinely fit. A coffee brand might get International Coffee Day; a B2B software company won't get Valentine's Day.
thematic_calendar.s10: Only moments that make sense for your brand are included. Generic filler is automatically skipped.
thematic_calendar.s12: Upcoming moments with suggested angles — how your brand could authentically tie into each one. For example:
thematic_calendar.s16: — angle: share your perspective on the key themes
thematic_calendar.s19: The planner decides whether a timely moment genuinely fits a given week. If it doesn't fit, it's not forced — a random holiday post for an unrelated brand is worse than no post at all.

weekly_recap.s4: Weekly Recap: a Monday email with your performance stats, trends, and suggestions.
weekly_recap.s8: Every Monday morning, you get an email telling you what happened last week, what's trending in your niche, and what you should do next. It's your brand's weekly check-in.
weekly_recap.s11: — how many posts were published, scheduled, or are still waiting for your approval
weekly_recap.s13: — likes, comments, shares, views — compared to the previous week, broken down by platform
weekly_recap.s15: — the most recent published post with its performance
weekly_recap.s17: — things that need your attention: pending posts, disconnected accounts, expired plans
weekly_recap.s21: — 3-5 topics relevant to your industry that you could post about, with real sources
weekly_recap.s23: — 3-5 actionable improvements based on your recent performance
weekly_recap.s24: The trends are grounded in real web data — not generic advice. They're tailored to your brand, audience, and current strategy.
weekly_recap.s26: Every week, Anomalia reviews what worked and what didn't across your recent posts. Patterns in what you approve, edit, or reject feed back into Brand Memory — so next week's content is even more aligned with your voice and preferences.
weekly_recap.s28: if you manage multiple brands, you get a separate recap for each one.

credits.s1: How Anomalia credits work, API value by plan, and chat rate limits (5-hour and weekly windows).
credits.s5: Credits meter AI usage across Anomalia. Paid plans also include rolling chat windows so a single burst of conversation can’t burn the whole month in one sitting.
credits.s7: Every AI action spends credits from your brand’s monthly allowance. Credits reset with your billing period.
credits.s10: How much a single action spends depends on what it asks for: a short chat reply is a few credits, a long article with its images is many more. The meter follows the work itself, not a fixed price per action.
credits.s18: Chat has two extra ceilings on top of the monthly quota. They only count
credits.s20: (and chat compaction). Autopilot, Studio, blog, Radar, SEO, and other tools spend monthly credits only — they do not fill these windows.
credits.s23: : we look at the last 5 hours and the last 7 days from now. If you hit a limit, chat pauses until enough older spend ages out — the UI shows the exact resume time (e.g. “You can resume at 14:30”).
credits.s28: Messages you send in brand chat, plus background compaction of long threads.
credits.s30: Editorial plan, Studio generation, blog articles, Radar, SEO/GEO, automations, and other non-chat AI.
credits.s32: Every chat turn also deducts from your monthly credit balance.
credits.s39: Higher tiers unlock capabilities — autopublish, connected social accounts, more Radar sources — on top of the larger credit allowance.
credits.s40: Annual billing does not change your monthly credits.

mcp.s10: Connect coding agents to Anomalia via Model Context Protocol. Same OAuth as the CLI — no static API tokens.
mcp.s14: Anomalia exposes a Model Context Protocol server so coding agents (Cursor, Claude, and others) can manage brands, posts, plans, studio, SEO/GEO, and blog — with the same OAuth login as the CLI.
mcp.s16: Authentication is always OAuth (browser login or Bearer from your session).
mcp.s18: Pick a transport: local stdio is simplest on your machine; remote HTTP is for cloud hosts.
mcp.s20: Best for Cursor and other local agents.
mcp.s21: Install Bun and clone the anomalia repo (or install the CLI binary so anomalia-mcp is on your PATH).

mcp.s29: Expect a JSON health payload with ok: true and mcp: "/mcp".
mcp.s31: Clients that speak MCP OAuth (opencode, Claude Code, Cursor, the Inspector…) authenticate on their own: on first connect they open anomalia.so, you approve, and the token is stored by the client. The initial 401 is the start of that handshake, not a crash.
mcp.s32: Custom option — if your client cannot do OAuth, attach the token by hand: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>, using the Supabase access token that anomalia login saves in ~/.config/anomalia/session.json. Static API keys (anomalia_…) are not accepted by the remote server.
mcp.s34: Auth: Bearer or the local session file.
mcp.s48: Prefer specific tools (approve_posts, edit_post, …) over chat for precise actions
mcp.s49: Post and article ids accept short unambiguous prefixes from list results (same rule as the CLI).
